prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: Across the five frames, the bright lower-edge regions place the camera wearer’s hands, torso, and legs roughly 0.2–1 m away, while the grass and other people are progressively darker and appear roughly 1–3 m away. Other people move from being mostly clipped at the upper edge to appearing ahead and slightly left/right of the wearer; they remain approximately 1–2 m apart, although monocular intensity cannot establish metric distances precisely. The map makes foreground/background separation, approach into the near field, and partial occlusion by the wearer’s body clearer than RGB, but it provides little reliable evidence for facing direction or gaze. Depth boundaries bleed around limbs, some background patches have inconsistent brightness, and cropped people near the top edge are especially unreliable.
descriptions.segmentation: The masks isolate several people from the grass: the camera wearer occupies the lower foreground, while other people are ahead and often partly cut off by the upper or side edges. Across the sequence, two standing people become more fully visible about 1–3 m ahead and roughly 1–2 m from each other, with one generally left of the other; small foreground objects visible in RGB are mostly unlabelled. The map makes person count, overlap, partial visibility, and left/right layout clearer than RGB, including thin arm and hand regions that merge visually with shadows. Mask fragments, missed body parts, changing instance colours, and small false or incomplete regions make exact distance, facing direction, gaze, and arm’s-reach judgments unreliable.
descriptions.pose: The pose map detects only hands in the early frames, placing the camera wearer’s hands in the near lower field at roughly 0.3–0.8 m, then detects two upper-body skeletons ahead in later frames at approximately 1–3 m. The yellow skeletons show those people separated left-to-right and oriented obliquely relative to the wearer, but missing or unstable head landmarks prevent a reliable claim that either looks directly toward the camera. Magenta hand detections reveal hands entering or leaving the field and indicate when a hand is near the wearer, while no clear hand-to-person contact or dependable shared arm’s-reach relationship is shown. The map clarifies limb configuration and turning across frames, but severe truncation, missing legs and torsos, floating keypoints, and occasional tiny false hand detections make occluded or edge-of-frame poses unreliable.
